summary: Implemented and specified V4 position sizing in USDG terms. Delivered the spec doc at docs/spec/strategy/V4_POSITION_SIZING.md, the integer-only sizing module at src/robinhood_lp/protocol/sizing.py (re-exported via src/robinhood_lp/protocol/__init__.py), pinned Solidity-derived integer vectors at tests/fixtures/strategy/position_sizing_vectors.json, and a 55-test suite at tests/test_position_sizing_t049.py. The implementation maps a fixed approved (tickLower, tickUpper) and a per-side raw-token capital envelope to one canonical integer liquidityDelta plus the mint envelope (amount0Max, amount1Max, deadline, minLiquidity), or to a structured NO_TRADE verdict with a stable reason code (RANGE_DEGENERATE / PRICE_OUT_OF_BOUNDS / CAP_NONPOSITIVE / CAP_UNDERFLOW / HOOK_DELTA_NONZERO_UNVERIFIED / GAS_RESERVE_UNDERFLOW / INSUFFICIENT_ECONOMIC_SIZE / USDG_CONVERSION_FAILED). All math is integer-only (ADR-004); the single Q64.64 USDG → raw-token conversion lives at usdg_amount_to_token_amount and never enters the float domain. The cap-bounded liquidity uses bracket-specific inverses (L0 = amount0 * pa * p / ((p - pa) << 96) for the inside-Range token0 bracket, L1 = amount1 << 96 / (pb - p) for the inside-Range token1 bracket) so the round-trip amounts_for_liquidity ∘ liquidity_for_amounts respects both caps — this differs from V4's reference getLiquidityForAmounts which uses asymmetric brackets and lets the round-trip exceed the supplied caps. Acceptance: pinned vectors cover below/inside/above-Range rounding and boundary prices; lowering either cap strictly reduces (or holds) liquidity and never moves the Range (must-not change Range to fit a cap); the simulated post-settlement wallet respects both caps and the native ETH Gas reservation (must-not spend Gas reserve); insufficient economic size returns NO_TRADE; an unverified hook is rejected; Hook BalanceDelta is added to the required amounts and verified per-side (must-not ignore Hook deltas). The module is float-free throughout (must-not size with float/display values); integers and uint128/uint256 widths are enforced at the boundary.

commands.result: 55 passed in 0.07s — pinned-vector matching for below/inside/above Range amounts and worst-case single-sided inventory at the boundaries; cap-bounded liquidity vectors for symmetric, asymmetric, below-only, and above-only cases; USDG → token conversion (round_down_one_to_one, round_down_ten_per_three, price_doubles_token_halves); monotonicity of lowering either cap; tick-alignment, range-degenerate, price-out-of-bounds, both-caps-zero, and simulated-settlement invariants; hook deltas (verified charge funded / verified charge exceeds cap → NO_TRADE / verified credit reduces required / unverified → SizingHookError / credit larger than position → SizingHookError); native Gas reservation (subtracts once from native-side cap / ignored when not native / underflow → NO_TRADE / exact-match → NO_TRADE); NO_TRADE insufficient economic size and the passing minimum-economic-size case; deterministic SizingDecision; float-free module surface; stable ReasonCode strings; SizingDecision invariants.

1429 passed, 6 skipped, 1 deselected in 13.74s. The 6 skips are pre-existing (Foundry drift / GPG verification / unsorted-currencies vector). The single deselected test fails because tools/oracle/lib/{v4-core,v4-periphery} git submodules are not initialised in this worktree — a pre-existing environment issue, not a T049-introduced defect; it is included in the parent /home/lpdev/lp checkout where the submodules exist. None of the new T049 tests skip or are deselected.
All checks passed! Zero lint findings across src/ and tests/.

residual_risks: V4 reference library bracket asymmetry: the existing get_liquidity_for_amounts helper in src/robinhood_lp/protocol/math.py uses V4's reference asymmetric brackets [p, pb] for token0 and [pa, p] for token1 when computing the inverse inside-Range; this implementation intentionally deviates from that behaviour because V4's round-trip can produce an amount that exceeds the supplied cap. The deviation is documented in compute_cap_bounded_liquidity and is the reason for the new spec; downstream consumers (T051 features.position, T065 strategy.usdg_range, T091 execution V4 transaction planner) must use the new sizing helpers, not the existing get_liquidity_for_amounts, for inside-Range sizing.

Hook BalanceDelta evidence: the implementation accepts a per-side hook_delta* when hook_verified=True; the verification gate is a boolean supplied by the caller. T043 is the source of per-pool verified evidence (verified vs unverified hook semantics), and the sizer assumes T043 has populated hook_verified correctly. A pool with T043='unverified' must call compute_sizing with hook_verified=False and hook_delta0=hook_delta1=0; the contract's HOOK_DELTA_NONZERO_UNVERIFIED path raises SizingHookError in that case.

USDG conversion boundary: usdg_amount_to_token_amount uses Q64.64 fixed-point arithmetic. The price input (price_q64_64) is supplied by T053 in V1; the implementation is a consumer of that contract. A T053 outage that sets price_q64_64=0 is rejected at the boundary (SizingUsdgConversionError); a misreporting price that rounds the USDG cap to zero in the wrong direction would produce a CAP_UNDERFLOW outcome and is not a T049 regression.

insufficient_economic_size gate: _liquidity_to_usdg_equivalent is a linear projection against the caller-supplied USDG amounts; the gate is conservative (linear) but not exact. The full USDG valuation belongs to T053. The T049 gate is sufficient for the 'final simulated settlement stays below both raw-token/USDG caps' acceptance clause.

Float-free audit is module-scoped (vars(sizing_module) inspection): the test ensures no float values are exported from sizing.py. The wider protocol package's float-free invariant is owned by ADR-009 and verified by the existing T012 acceptance. T049 does not change ADR-009.

The same test passes in /home/lpdev/lp. The T049 implementation does not depend on this test.
